runs.reason:
**Base rate.** Dell raised its full-year revenue midpoint at one of its last two comparable Q3 reports: it lowered the midpoint in FY2025, then raised it from $107.0 billion to $111.7 billion in FY2026. That’s a useful starting point, but two reports are too few to establish a stable rate. ([investors.delltechnologies.com](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/_assets/_2d115b668eb9569931e94aa91d9c5fb3/delltechnologies/db/3595/34515/webcast_transcript/DELL_Q3FY25_Earnings_Transcript.pdf))

**What moves this case.**
- **Toward YES:** On September 1, Dell reported $47.0 billion in Q2 revenue, above the $45.0 billion top of its prior range. It also reported $60.9 billion in AI-server orders and a $95 billion backlog. Dell has orders to support a further raise if it can ship more than it assumed in September. ([investors.delltechnologies.com](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1653/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial-results))
- **Against YES:** The same September update had already lifted the full-year midpoint by $25 billion to exactly $192.0 billion. Dell identified DRAM and NAND availability as constraints, and November 20 reporting still flagged memory as a risk. The backlog supports demand, but it doesn’t establish how much Dell can ship this fiscal year. ([investors.delltechnologies.com](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1653/dell-technologies-delivers-second-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial-results))
- **Modestly toward YES:** November previews put Q3 revenue consensus at $49.2 billion to about $50.2 billion, versus Dell’s $49.0 billion midpoint. That points toward a beat, but even a beat would not force a full-year raise if Q4 expectations weaken. ([kiplinger.com](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/stocks/17494/next-week-earnings-calendar-stocks))

**Timing.** Dell’s November 10 announcement says it will publish results and guidance before its November 24 call at 4:30 p.m. ET. I assign about a 1% chance that it does not publish on the required date. ([investors.delltechnologies.com](https://investors.delltechnologies.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1661/dell-technologies-to-hold-conference-call-nov-24-to-discuss-third-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial-results))

While rising component costs primarily threaten gross margins rather than top-line revenue, supply chain bottlenecks or customer deployment delays could limit how quickly Dell converts its $95 billion backlog into recognized Q3 and Q4 revenue.

### (3) Strongest Reason the Obvious Outcome Might Fail
The current $192.0 billion full-year guide (after $43.8 billion in Q1 and $47.0 billion in Q2, and assuming $49.0 billion in Q3) already implies an aggressive $52.2 billion fourth quarter, requiring AI server shipments to average roughly $20.7 billion per quarter in the second half (up 26% over Q2's record $16.4 billion). If data center readiness or component supply constraints (such as high-bandwidth memory or next-generation GPU availability) caused Q3 shipments to merely meet the $49.0 billion target—or if management tempers Q4 PC and traditional server expectations—Dell could simply reaffirm its $192.0 billion midpoint rather than raise it further. There is also a very small procedural risk (under 3%) that Dell omits the full-year number from the main press release text and puts it only in the presentation deck, though its phrasing in the Nov 10 announcement ("via a press release with accompanying financial statements and guidance") and its consistent format over the last year make that unlikely.

Weighing the massive $95 billion order backlog, the pattern of three consecutive massive beats and raises, and the fact that current guidance is already at $192.0 billion against the already steep implied second-half ramp, I estimate a 75% chance that Dell raises its full-year revenue guidance above $192.0 billion on November 24.

In its Q2 fiscal 2027 financial results press release, Dell reported record Q2 revenue of $47.0 billion, record AI server orders of $60.9 billion, a $95 billion AI server backlog, and raised its full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance by $25 billion to $192.0 billion.

Dell Technologies announced it will hold a conference call on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, at 3:30 p.m. CST to discuss its Q3 fiscal 2027 results, and will issue the results and guidance via press release before the call.
Dell's Q3 fiscal 2027 revenue guidance set on September 1 is $49.0 billion, while analyst consensus estimates stand higher at $49.25 billion (arincen) and $50.63 billion (Earnings Whispers).

Hitting Dell's existing $192.0 billion full-year revenue guide and $74.0 billion AI server guide already implies roughly $20.7 billion per quarter in second-half AI server sales (26% above Q2's $16.4 billion) and $52.2 billion in total Q4 revenue after a $49.0 billion Q3.

runs.reason:
Dell has raised full-year revenue guidance at the Q3 report in a prior year of AI-driven demand (FY26, to a $111.7 billion midpoint) and has already raised the FY27 figure twice this year, from a $140 billion midpoint in February to $167 billion in May and then to $192.0 billion in September. Conditional on large backlogs and recent beats, the base rate of a further increase at a late-year print is therefore above 50 percent, though not automatic: historical guidance updates overall have been split between raises and cuts, and companies often reaffirm rather than lift when only one quarter remains.

The September raise left a $95 billion AI-server backlog and an implied second-half pace that already assumes acceleration. Consensus and at least one sell-side note (17 November) look for a Q3 revenue beat versus the $49 billion guide and explicitly anticipate another full-year lift, potentially past $200 billion if AI-server shipments reach roughly $85 billion. Offsetting that, memory and other component shortages have been the binding constraint all year, and reporting on 22 November describes Dell seeking large price increases on already-signed AI-server contracts, including an ongoing lawsuit, which can slow conversion or prompt caution on Q4.

The more likely outcome is therefore a modest raise whose midpoint sits above $192.0 billion, but the margin is not wide.
